stories.title: In Commercial Real Estate, a Plausible Answer From AI Is Not Enough
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence can now produce work that looks remarkably finished. It can summarize a lease, review a rent roll, draft an investment committee memo and explain a change in occupancy in polished language. That creates a new problem for commercial real estate firms: A document can look ready long before it is safe to use. For an asset manager, controller or acquisitions professional, the test is not whether an answer reads well but whether the person receiving it can defend the work. Where did the number come from? Was it pulled from the current rent roll or an older version? Does “occupancy” mean leased, physically occupied or economically occupied? Were the calculations independently checked? What happens when the system is unsure? Arunabh Dastidar. Photo: Courtesy Leni. Those questions are becoming more important as AI moves beyond drafting and begins completing longer sequences of work. Consider a routine request: “Send the Monday operating report.” To a person, that instruction carries a great deal of unstated knowledge. The report must use the correct reporting period, property list and accounting data. It may need to flag certain variances but ignore others. Some information may be available to the asset management team, but restricted from other recipients. The finished document may also require review before it leaves the company. The request sounds like one task. In practice, it is a series of decisions. That distinction matters because each individual step can appear reasonable while the final result is wrong. An AI system may retrieve a document, summarize it, add figures to a spreadsheet and prepare an email. But, if it selects an outdated file or sends the report to the wrong distribution list, the fact that every individual step worked correctly offers little comfort. stories.title: Wells Fargo Provides $175M Construction Loan for Queens Mixed-Use Development
stories.excerpt: The affordable housing development push continues in New York City. The Domain Companies has secured $175 million in construction financing to build Elara, a two-building, 429-unit mixed-income housing development in the historic Astoria neighborhood of Queens, Commercial Observer can first report. Wells Fargo provided the construction debt, while Domain Companies contributed an undisclosed amount of equity into the deal together with Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management. JLL Capital Markets’ Chris Peck and Nicco Lupo arranged the transaction. In a statement, Jacob Feingold, partner and head of originations at Canyon Partners Real Estate, cited Astoria’s ongoing population growth and The Domain Companies’ experience building in the area. The firm opened Jasper, a 499-unit multifamily complex along the Queens waterfront, in 2025. “We continue to see attractive opportunities to invest in high-quality residential projects in markets supported by strong housing demand and compelling long-term fundamentals,” said Feingold. Located at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in an area that borders the neighborhoods of Sunnyside Gardens and Astoria, Elara is split between Elara East, an 18-story building with 330 apartments, and Elara West, a 12-story building with 99 apartments. Between the two buildings, the complex will deliver 107 permanently affordable housing units and 4,000 square feet of retail space. On-site amenities will include fitness centers, co-working spaces, a screening room, a gaming room with a golf simulator, a children’s playroom, a dog wash station and outdoor courtyards, while Elara East will hold a rooftop terrace with views of the Manhattan skyline. bullets: Wells Fargo funds $175M construction loan for Domain Companies' 429-unit Elara in Queens Astoria
Mixed-income development follows Domain's 499-unit Jasper waterfront completion in early 2025
Strong housing demand and population growth cited as underwriting drivers in Queens
stories.summary: Domain Companies secured $175 million in construction financing from Wells Fargo for Elara, a two-building, 429-unit mixed-income development in Astoria, Queens, with equity from Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management. The deal reflects continued affordable housing development momentum in NYC and follows Domain's successful 2025 delivery of Jasper, a 499-unit complex on the Queens waterfront. Lender and equity partners cited Astoria's population growth and strong housing fundamentals as core underwriting drivers.
stories.impact: Queens waterfront and Astoria submarkets show sustained rental demand strength sufficient to attract institutional capital (Wells Fargo, Canyon Partners) into mixed-income product. Domain's back-to-back deliveries signal operator confidence in the borough's absorbability; developers should monitor Astoria-LIC rent growth and occupancy trends to time future acquisitions ahead of further population in-migration.

stories.title: Architecture and Design Firm SWA Group Inks 6K SF at 381 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: Architecture and design firm SWA Group has signed a 5,789-square-foot lease at Olmstead Properties’ 381 Park Avenue South in Midtown South, the landlord announced Tuesday. The 10.5-year lease for the global landscape architecture, planning and urban design firm will stretch across part of the building’s 12th floor. SWA — which did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment — will relocate from 31 West 27th Street. The exact asking rent was not disclosed, but Olmstead did note that asking rent in the building averages $75 per square foot. SWA was represented by Janet Liff from J. Liff Co., while Steve Marvin and Jonathan Bock from Olmstead Properties represented ownership in the deal. Liff did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. Meanwhile, Olmstead also announced Tuesday that health care products company On The Right Track Systems, backed by Riveria Investment Group, signed a new lease for 4,157 square feet on part of the 10th floor of 381 Park Avenue South, relocating from 99 Park Avenue. Riveria invested in the provider of proprietary hospital privacy curtains and health care industry track systems in February 2025. The lease runs for seven years and six months. Olmstead’s Marvin and Bock also represented ownership in that deal, while the tenant was represented by Arash Sadighi and Tyler Ruggieri from Venture Commercial NYC, as well as by Alan Rosinsky from Metro Manhattan Office Space. Olmstead has been seeing strong leasing momentum at 381 Park Avenue South as well as 373 Park Avenue South, bringing the two properties to about 99,000 square feet of new office and retail leases in the past eight months. stories.title: B of A Pays $155M for Jacksonville Office Buildings
stories.excerpt: Bank of America paid $155 million for five buildings and two parking garages that it had been leasing at its Southside Boulevard operations center campus. The banking giant acquired the property from Ladder Capital of New York City. Bank of America bought about 820,000 square feet of space spanning Buildings 200, 300, 400, 500 and 600 at the campus at 9000 Southside Blvd., north of The Avenues mall. The company has invested heavily in renovating the properties it bought. As part of the transaction, Bank of America will continue to lease about 78,000 square feet across three floors in Building 100, which is owned by Glenfield Capital of Atlanta. The Southside campus serves as one of Bank of America’s major operations hubs and supports more than 7,100 employees across its businesses, including consumer banking, wealth management, operations, technology, and staff and support functions. Bank of America remains the largest bank in metro Jacksonville with 23 branches. The post B of A Pays $155M for Jacksonville Office Buildings appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.title: Florida Panthers, Broward County Exploring Entertainment District
stories.excerpt: Broward County has submitted plans that could transform the 154-acre area surrounding the Florida Panthers’ home into a massive 24/7 mixed-use destination in Sunrise. The Panthers say they’re in the early stages of discussions with Broward County and Sunrise. A Sunrise City Commission will consider the proposal next week. The proposal could include 1,400 apartments, 600 hotel rooms, 1.62 million square feet of office/education space and 300,000 square feet of commercial space. Much of the development replaces portions of the current parking lots. It’s not known if the Amerant Bank Arena will be part of the transformation. Major sports stadiums and arenas across the United States are increasingly paired with mixed-use entertainment districts. Prominent examples include The Battery Atlanta at Truist Park, Ballpark Village at Busch Stadium in St. Louis, and L.A. Live across from where the Los Angeles Lakers play basketball. The post Florida Panthers, Broward County Exploring Entertainment District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Broward County proposes 1,400 apartments + 600 hotel rooms around Florida Panthers arena in Sunrise
154-acre mixed-use entertainment district replaces parking, adds 1.62M SF office/education and 300K SF retail

stories.summary: Broward County has submitted a transformation plan for the 154-acre area surrounding the Florida Panthers' Amerant Bank Arena in Sunrise, proposing 1,400 apartments, 600 hotel rooms, 1.62 million square feet of office/education space, and 300,000 square feet of commercial uses, with much of the development replacing surface parking. The Panthers and local government are in early discussions; Sunrise City Commission will consider the proposal imminently. The concept mirrors successful stadium-anchored mixed-use districts like The Battery Atlanta and Ballpark Village.
stories.impact: This arena-anchored project would create a significant rental demand catalyst in the Sunrise/Broward submarket by concentrating workers, visitors, and residents around a major entertainment/employment anchor. If approved and financed, it represents a 1,400-unit supply inflow; developers should track entitlement timing and pre-leasing signals to assess whether competing projects should advance or delay starts. The model also signals that parking-heavy suburban campuses in South Florida are now developable as mixed-use infill.

stories.title: ApartmentIQ Secures $25M Follow-On Funding Round
stories.excerpt: Multifamily data company ApartmentIQ announced Tuesday that it has secured a $25 million follow-on funding round. Susquehanna Growth Equity (SGE) funded the follow-on after leading ApartmentIQ’s $22.5 million Series B financing in 2021, when the company was known as Rentable, a large national apartment marketplace. ApartmentIQ — which now bills itself as a real-time market intelligence, revenue management and AI platform for the multifamily sector — also announced that it had surpassed 8 million units in its customer base. “We are taking the data that powers our market survey platform we’ve been collecting and adding additional products,” said Alec Slocum, co-founder and CEO of ApartmentIQ about the follow-on founding round’s timing. “There’s two additional products that we’ve launched in the last nine months based on that same data. We call the first one Explore Pro, which is a market research tool used by acquisitions asset management teams to figure out where they should buy, build and redevelop. The second product we’ve launched is called Daylight. It’s a revenue management tool that’s powered by the public data that we’ve collected.” Alec Slocum. PHOTO: Courtesy ApartmentIQ Both products are currently tracking to surpass 1 million customer units in their first year. The SGE capital also triggered the launch of MavenAI, ApartmentIQ’s multifamily marketing agent, which represents the company’s first major step into agentic AI. MavenAI uses software to uncover insights and take action on behalf of operators, according to the company. bullets: ApartmentIQ raises $25M Series C led by Susquehanna Growth Equity; surpasses 8 million units tracked
Launched Explore Pro (acquisition/asset management tool) and Daylight (revenue management) in past 9 months
Real-time market intelligence and AI platform increasingly central to multifamily underwriting workflows
stories.summary: ApartmentIQ, a multifamily data and revenue management platform formerly known as Rentable, secured $25 million in Series C funding from Susquehanna Growth Equity, which also led the company's 2021 Series B at $22.5 million. The platform now covers 8 million units and has launched two new products in the past nine months: Explore Pro, a market research and site selection tool for acquisitions and asset management, and Daylight, a revenue management solution. CEO Alec Slocum emphasized the value of leveraging proprietary market survey data to power downstream products.
stories.impact: ApartmentIQ's funding and product velocity underscore that real-time market intelligence and AI-driven site selection are now table-stakes for institutional multifamily developers in underwriting and capital allocation. Explore Pro's traction suggests developer teams are increasingly relying on algorithmic/data-driven site selection over traditional broker and pro-forma analysis; teams without access to granular market data and predictive tools risk slower acquisition cycles and weaker conviction in site selection. This raises the cost of capital and competitive advantage for data-informed operators.

stories.title: JLB Pursuing Buckhead Office-to-Apartments Conversion
stories.excerpt: JLB Partners plans to redevelop a seven-story building at 470 E. Paces Ferry Road in Buckhead Village. The Atlanta Business Chronicle reports the project consists of 314 apartments in what was once a mid-century office building. On Maple Drive, the 1960s-era office building is the longtime home of Logility Supply Chain Solutions. Aptean acquired Logility in 2025 and has maintained a small workforce in the building. A shopping center is directly south of the site, and various businesses operate out of older homes along Shadowlawn Avenue to the west. Additional retail is located to the north along Peachtree Road. Other condo and apartment buildings have risen all over the area, including the Camden Buckhead Square and Ashley Gables Buckhead developments. Future residents would be within walking distance of Buckhead Village District, the upscale mixed-use development spanning multiple city blocks. Construction on the proposed development could begin in summer 2027, pending permitting approval. The post JLB Pursuing Buckhead Office-to-Apartments Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLB Partners converting 470 E. Paces Ferry Road (1960s office, 7-story) to 314 apartments in Buckhead
Longstanding tenant Logility acquired by Aptean in 2025; reduced workforce enables conversion
Construction targeted for summer 2027; walkable to Buckhead Village mixed-use district
stories.summary: JLB Partners is converting a seven-story, mid-century office building at 470 E. Paces Ferry Road in Buckhead Village to 314 apartments. The property was previously occupied by Logility Supply Chain Solutions, which was acquired by Aptean in 2025 and has since reduced its on-site workforce. Construction is targeted to begin in summer 2027 pending approvals. The site benefits from proximity to Buckhead Village District and other recent apartment and condo deliveries in the submarket.
stories.impact: Buckhead's office-to-residential conversion pipeline is accelerating as major employers (Aptean/Logility) downsize legacy office footprints. This conversion opportunity signals soft office demand in the submarket and rising residential values; developers should scout other occupied mid-rise office assets with tenant turnover risk or shrinking corporate tenants. JLB's timeline (summer 2027 start) suggests 2025–2026 permitting; monitor Buckhead entitlement trends to identify windows for competing conversion or ground-up projects before zoning tightens.

stories.title: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader, the Blockbuster New Firm in Corporate Law
stories.excerpt: You know that nightmare, where you are late for class and your teacher calls out from behind you, and all you feel is dread? That happened to real estate lawyer Sulie Arias, a partner with the corporate finance practice at Hogan Lovells Cadwalader — a newly formed firm thanks to a $3.9 billion merger — except her reality wasn’t a nightmare. The professor was running to catch up with Arias to tell the trembling student just how impressed she was with the grade Arias received on a test that very few people had even passed. The professor encouraged Arias to pursue law as a career, and now she is part of one of the biggest law firms in the country, working alongside people like Trevor Adler, another partner in the corporate finance practice. Hogan Lovells Cadwalader is the result of the almost $4 billion merger between Hogan Lovells, and Cadwalader Wickersham & Taft that took effect on July 1, creating a singular firm. Commercial Observer caught up with Arias and Adler in August to discuss the merger, their careers and practices, insights on office leasing and the other real estate markets in New York City, as well as the benefits of the merger. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Please introduce yourselves and tell us about your practice. Trevor Adler: I am from the legacy Hogan Lovell side. I am a lifer with my particular group of people. I started as a summer associate in 2006, and have been with the same real estate team ever since. There are a lot of lifers in our combined team too. I do all things real estate, but my specialty is condominiums and commercial leasing — office, retail, medical, data centers — on both the landlord and tenant side, about half my work is in the New York City area, and about half is across the country. stories.title: CBRE Scores Charleston-Area Warehouse Leasing Assignment
stories.excerpt: CBRE has been retained to market and lease North Rhett Center at 5801 North Rhett Avenue, a 516,000-square-foot two-building industrial property in Hanahan, South Carolina. The property offers approximately 318,926 square feet of available space for lease and was recently acquired by Obelisk Real Estate Partners. CBRE’s Brendan Redeyoff and Bob Barrineau are leading leasing efforts on behalf of Obelisk Real Estate Partners. Obelisk Real Estate Partners recently acquired 5801 North Rhett Avenue and the adjacent 305,250-square foot industrial property at 1020 North Pointe Industrial Boulevard from CenterPoint Properties. The available space at 5801 North Rhett can accommodate users ranging from approximately 50,000 square feet to the full 318,926 square feet. The property also offers CSX rail service and up to 3.25 acres of laydown yard space, providing flexibility for a range of manufacturing, logistics and distribution users. The asset is also proximate to the NIWC and Charleston International Airport, where Boeing is expanding its production facility. stories.title: High Street Residential Tops Out on First Manhattan Development
stories.excerpt: High Street Residential (HSR), the residential subsidiary of Trammell Crow Company, has topped out construction on the firm’s first Manhattan project, The Marq, a 25-story luxury residential tower in SoHo. Slated for completion in the fourth quarter of 2027, the project will include 99 units, 2,072 square feet of ground-floor retail and 25 affordable apartments. Located on a vacant lot at 126 Lafayette St. in New York City’s Lower West Side, units at The Marq will range from studios to three-bedroom penthouses. “Our aim is for The Marq to reflect the vibrancy and elegance of this iconic community of SoHo,” said Michael Adamo, a principal with HSR in New York. “With its proximity to major transit hubs and green spaces like Hudson River Park, SoHo remains one of New York City’s most desirable locations for residential development. We’re proud to bring this project to life.” Along with its capital partners, other project partners on The Marq include Marvel Architects, general contractor Leeding Builders Group and interior designer Chris Shao Studio. bullets: High Street Residential (Trammell Crow Co. subsidiary) topped out The Marq, 25-story luxury tower in SoHo Manhattan
99 units (studios to 3-bed penthouses) + 2,072 SF retail + 25 affordable apartments; completion Q4 2027
First Manhattan project for HSR; positioned on vacant lot at 126 Lafayette Street, Lower West Side
stories.summary: High Street Residential, the residential division of Trammell Crow Company, has reached topping-out on The Marq, a 25-story luxury residential tower in SoHo with 99 market-rate units (studios through three-bedroom penthouses), 25 affordable apartments, and 2,072 square feet of ground-floor retail. Located on a previously vacant parcel at 126 Lafayette Street on Manhattan's Lower West Side, the project is slated for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2027.
stories.impact: This flagship Manhattan entry by High Street Residential (a Trammell Crow subsidiary) validates SoHo-Lower West Side as investable ground-up luxury residential. The 99-unit density on a compact infill site and affordable unit inclusion (25 units, ~20% of mix) reflect current market/regulatory realities for Manhattan development. Completion in Q4 2027 means pre-leasing should begin in 2026–2027; performance and absorption data will inform whether Trammell Crow accelerates subsequent Manhattan/Tier-1 market development activity. Project viability also signals robust capital availability for luxury residential in prime Manhattan submarkets despite recent rate volatility.
